holidays.name: National Lost Sock Memorial Day
holidays.description: A day to mourn the single socks that vanished mysteriously from the dryer. Participants hold a mock memorial for their missing footwear and finally pair up the orphan socks lurking in their drawers.
holidays.origin: Created by Mitchell Rapp and Susan Rapp, who held a tongue-in-cheek memorial for lost socks and registered the day as a humorous observance.
holidays.funFact: Many people claim that the 'sock-eating dryer' phenomenon is real, yet the likeliest culprits are socks that get trapped behind the drum or stuck inside fitted sheets and pant legs.

holidays.name: National Butterscotch Brownie Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the chewy, golden-brown cousin of the chocolate brownie, also known as a blondie. Bakers whip up a batch and enjoy the buttery, caramel-like flavor.
holidays.origin: A food observance that grew out of the popularity of blondies, which date back to the early 20th century, though the exact creator of the day is unknown.
holidays.funFact: Butterscotch has no actual scotch in it. It is made from brown sugar and butter, and the 'scotch' likely comes from the word 'scorch' or 'score,' referring to how the candy was cut.

holidays.name: Moscow Victory Day Parade Anniversary / Victory Day
holidays.description: Commemorated across Russia and other former Soviet states with parades, fireworks, and the wearing of orange-and-black St. George ribbons to mark the end of World War II in Europe from the Soviet perspective.
holidays.origin: Germany's act of military surrender was signed late on May 8, 1945 in Central European time, which was already May 9 in Moscow, so the Soviet Union celebrates on May 9.
holidays.funFact: The time zone difference is the reason Russia celebrates a day later than most of Europe, who observe V-E Day on May 8.

holidays.name: Europe Day
holidays.description: A celebration of peace and unity in Europe, featuring open days at EU institutions, concerts, and parties. It is a day for people to explore the cultures of 27 member countries.
holidays.origin: It marks the anniversary of the 1950 Schuman Declaration, in which French foreign minister Robert Schuman proposed the pooling of coal and steel production, a step that led to the European Union.
holidays.funFact: The EU anthem is the 'Ode to Joy' from Beethoven's Ninth Symphony, performed without lyrics so it doesn't favor any one language.

holidays.name: Lost Sock Memorial Day Companion: Third Culture... Cheer Up the Lonely Day Spin-Off: National Ice Cream and Sock Hop Hour
holidays.description: Not an official holiday, but a popular tongue-in-cheek idea among sock memorial celebrants: pair a lone-sock ceremony with a retro sock hop and a scoop of ice cream.
holidays.origin: Born from social media jokes in which people suggested giving lost socks a proper send-off with a dance party.
holidays.funFact: The term 'sock hop' came from 1950s teen dances held in school gyms where kids took off their shoes to protect the polished floor.
